videos.title: Official trailer
videos.note: Wall-to-wall noise, close-ups and Oneohtrix synths. The trailer makes you feel Howard's panic, which is exactly the film's pitch.

videos.title: Official trailer
videos.note: Candy-coloured neon and dream logic. It sells a mood that's half party and half nightmare.

videos.title: Elevator scene
videos.note: The lights dim to a single glow for one kiss, then the scene snaps into brutal violence. A whole relationship turns in one confined space.

videos.title: Boat chase
videos.note: While the boat chase rages in the background, Solo sits in a truck eating a sandwich to an Italian love song. Ritchie at his coolest: action seen from a deadpan side angle.

videos.title: F/W26 campaign film
videos.note: A tight streetwear collab film. It shows how two brands share a frame without either one shouting over the other.

videos.title: "The Dreamer" holiday film
videos.note: Apple's annual holiday short: a small human story where the product is just the tool for the dream. A masterclass in letting the emotion sell.

videos.title: Territory
videos.note: A young man's homecoming in Algiers: rooftops, family and raw emotion. It won the Film Craft Grand Prix at Cannes Lions, and the band directed it themselves.

videos.title: Open Your World (long version)
videos.note: The Heineken Legend charms his way through an impossibly stylish night, to The Asteroids Galaxy Tour. Endless set pieces carried by one charismatic lead.

videos.title: Unskippable: Family
videos.note: The pitch is delivered before the skip button appears, then the family freezes while the dog eats dinner. It hacked the pre-roll format and won the Film Grand Prix at Cannes.

videos.title: "Morning Routine" title sequence
videos.note: Shaving, slicing fruit, tying shoelaces, all in extreme close-up so they read as violence. A mundane routine becomes a portrait of a killer.

videos.title: Bank robbery
videos.note: Masks, a note slid across the counter and a getaway that goes wrong in seconds. Tight close-ups and a pulsing synth score keep the panic in your chest.

videos.title: One-on-one with Chigurh
videos.note: An ordinary exchange becomes life or death in a few lines. No score, just pauses, and the threat lives entirely in performance.

videos.title: Pool party oner
videos.note: The camera drifts through a 70s pool party and dives underwater with a guest. One long move introduces a whole world of characters.

videos.title: 20th anniversary trailer
videos.note: Saturated reds, slow motion and that waltz. Proof a trailer can sell pure longing without explaining the story.

videos.title: One question away
videos.note: Night-time LA on early digital cameras and a cold, calm Tom Cruise. Mann turns a simple exchange into dread.

videos.title: "A land of wolves"
videos.note: A quiet line delivered in shadow says more than any action beat. Villeneuve and Deakins let silence and framing carry the threat.

videos.title: Official trailer
videos.note: Spinning cameras, neon colour and a wall-to-wall soundtrack. A trailer cut like a music video that shifts tone halfway through.

videos.title: "Smoking kills": Johnny Quid
videos.note: Johnny Quid's swaggering monologue: Ritchie dialogue at its most quotable, delivered with total confidence.

videos.title: Opening sequence
videos.note: The camera pulls out from inside the narrator's brain, along neurons, to a gun in his mouth. A CG title sequence that is also the first story beat.

videos.title: From diner to driver
videos.note: A crew's quiet professionalism told through a diner meeting and a drive. Mann makes restraint look cool.

videos.title: Copacabana oner
videos.note: One unbroken Steadicam move through the kitchen into the club. The camera itself shows the power Henry is selling to Karen.

videos.title: Butch meets Vincent
videos.note: Two men size each other up at a bar with barely a line spoken. Tarantino stages menace through framing and silence.

videos.title: Transamerica building timelapse
videos.note: Fincher marks the passage of years with the Transamerica Pyramid rising in timelapse over a black screen. A time jump turned into a single striking image.

videos.brand: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
videos.title: Official trailer
videos.note: Period radio, sun-drenched LA and a cast introduced like movie stars. A trailer that sells a mood and an era more than a plot.

videos.title: Official trailer
videos.note: Quiet, patient and built on looks rather than lines. Proof that a trailer can be gentle and still land hard.

videos.title: Official trailer
videos.note: A relationship drama that turns into body horror, cut with escalating dread. NEON trailer craft at its sharpest.

videos.title: Corridor fight
videos.note: One side-scrolling take down a corridor, one man with a hammer against dozens. Exhaustion is part of the choreography.

videos.title: Ending scene
videos.note: The famous ambiguous ending: Travis in the cab, a glance in the rearview mirror. A few seconds that re-frame everything before them.

videos.title: "Sell me this pen" / recruiting scene
videos.note: Jordan recruits his friends with a pitch demonstration that is half sermon, half comedy. Energy and rhythm as the whole sell.

videos.title: Official trailer #2
videos.note: A family drama trailer built on faces and a house full of history. Restrained cutting lets the performances sell it.

videos.title: Burning caravan scene
videos.note: Slow motion, Oasis-style melancholy over a burning caravan: Ritchie flips a revenge beat into something almost beautiful. Music against action is the whole trick.

videos.title: MKC "Bull"
videos.note: Almost more pauses than words: McConaughey sits in the car facing down a bull. Refn proves an ad can be pure mood and still sell the brand.

videos.title: SS21 campaign
videos.note: A fashion campaign treated like a Guadagnino film: lingering looks, warm light, no hard sell. Hire a film director and let them shoot their world.

videos.title: Opening scene
videos.note: A rapid-fire breakup conversation sets up the entire character in five minutes. Sorkin's rhythm plus Fincher's precise coverage.

videos.title: Business cards scene
videos.note: Grown men sweat over typefaces and paper stock. Extreme close-ups and silence make something trivial feel murderous.

videos.title: Opening title sequence
videos.note: Hand-lettered credits over B-52s refuelling mid-air to "Try a Little Tenderness". Loose, imperfect type set the satirical tone and inspired a thousand hand-drawn sequences.

videos.title: Art gallery scene
videos.note: Three kids from the estates crash a Paris gallery opening. Class clash played for awkward comedy that turns sour, shot in crisp black and white.

videos.title: Naming Mr. Pink
videos.note: A crime crew argues about code names like it's life or death. Tarantino builds character through bickering, not exposition.

videos.title: Final trailer
videos.note: Rain, neon and slow menace carry the franchise look into a new series. Study how the cut leans on texture and sound rather than plot.

videos.title: Night raid scene
videos.note: A night raid told through thermal and night-vision POV with almost no music. Restraint and sound design do the work.

videos.title: Opening credits
videos.note: Scratched film, jittery hand-made type and Nine Inch Nails turn the credits into the killer's notebook. Titles can do character work before a single line of dialogue.

videos.title: Opening title sequence
videos.note: A heavy multigenerational drama opens with its whole cast dancing in a neon pachinko parlor. Contrast between tone of the show and tone of the titles is what makes it unforgettable.

videos.title: A Tale As Old As Websites (extended)
videos.note: Barry Keoghan delivers websites door to door in rural Ireland like a paperboy. A single absurd premise, shot with indie-film restraint, carries the whole spot.

videos.title: Time-traveling blues scene
videos.note: One song bends time: past and future musicians join a juke-joint performance in a single flowing move. A blueprint for letting music drive camera and edit.

videos.title: Opening title sequence
videos.note: Extreme close-ups of an eye dissolve into hypnotic spirals over Bernard Herrmann's score. Proof that a few graphic shapes can set the whole psychological tone.

videos.title: Season 1 opening credits
videos.note: Double exposures fuse faces with refineries and swamps, so the characters literally contain the landscape. A strong single visual device, repeated with discipline.

videos.title: Italian accents scene
videos.note: Comedy and lethal tension in the same breath: bad Italian accents in front of a man who speaks it perfectly. Study how long Tarantino holds the discomfort.

videos.title: The drugs kick in
videos.note: The grade warms and sharpens the moment the pill hits, and text floats off the page. A clean example of showing a mental change purely through image.

videos.title: Official trailer
videos.note: Kinetic handheld, freeze frames and a samba-driven cut. The trailer sells pace and attitude before story.

videos.title: Season 1 opening credits
videos.note: Waves, school runs and sideways glances cut to "Cold Little Heart". The calm surface hides the threat, exactly like the show.
The product never appears. One symbolic act (the hammer through the screen) carries the whole brand promise. Build your next spot around a single image that means something, not a feature list.

videos.title: Think Different
videos.note: A manifesto VO over a black-and-white portrait montage. With AI, create archetype portraits (the inventor, the rebel) in a consistent B&W grade and cut them to one spoken rhythm.

videos.title: Welcome Home
videos.note: A tiny apartment physically stretches and unfolds to the music. Push this: let the set react to the beat. Generate the room states as keyframes and morph between them on downbeats.

videos.title: Sway
videos.note: Earbuds in, the world dissolves into a private duet in the snow. Classic structure: ordinary moment → music kicks in → fantasy → back to reality with a smile.

videos.title: Bounce
videos.note: Pavement turns to trampoline. One impossible physics rule held for the whole spot. Simple to prompt, very visual, easy to sustain across shots.

videos.title: Privacy — Data Auction
videos.note: An abstract idea (data being sold) made literal as a live auction. Turn the invisible problem your product solves into a physical scene.

videos.title: The Greatest
videos.note: Real use cases cut to an anthem track, each vignette a 3–5 second micro-story. Good template for a 60–90s montage: every shot needs its own tiny payoff.

videos.title: Crush!
videos.note: A hydraulic press crushes instruments and art into an iPad. Visually precise, but people hated what it said. Study it as a warning: a destruction metaphor can read as contempt for craft.

videos.title: Fuzzy Feelings
videos.note: A stop-motion look with felt textures and a tiny office worker. AI tools can fake this tactile style: prompt fabric, fuzz and slight frame-to-frame jitter.

videos.title: The Surprise
videos.note: A quiet build to one emotional reveal that the product makes possible. The product is the delivery device, not the hero.

videos.title: Share Your Gifts
videos.note: An animated short about a shy creator. Characters plus a clear emotional arc in 2 minutes: want, fear, push, release.

videos.title: Dream Crazy
videos.note: A VO-led montage where each line pays off on screen right away. Write the VO first, then generate one exact visual per line.

videos.title: You Can't Stop Us
videos.note: Split-screen match cuts: two athletes, one continuous motion across the frame. Perfect for AI: generate pairs of clips with matching poses and camera moves.

videos.title: Write the Future
videos.note: One mistake or win spins into a fast-forward of possible futures. A branching 'what if' structure packs huge scale into 3 minutes.

videos.title: Find Your Greatness (The Jogger)
videos.note: One locked-off shot of a kid jogging toward camera, with a calm VO. Proof that one strong image and one sentence can beat 40 cuts.

videos.title: The Last Game
videos.note: Stylized 3D animation: footballers against perfect clones. The 'humans vs. soulless perfection' theme fits an AI filmmaker very well.

videos.title: Winning Isn't for Everyone
videos.note: An antihero voice ('am I a bad person?') over intense athlete close-ups. Flip the expected sentiment and let the tone carry it.

videos.title: So Win
videos.note: Contrast built line by line: 'you're told you can't X… so win'. A repeatable copy structure you can apply to any brand.

videos.title: Nothing Beats a Londoner
videos.note: Kids one-up each other in a relay where each scene hands off to the next. The 'escalating hand-off' structure keeps energy rising.

videos.title: Dream Crazier
videos.note: Reclaiming an insult as a rallying cry. Split-screen and archival-style textures with one strong VO.

videos.title: Impossible Is Nothing
videos.note: Short declarative lines over hero athlete moments. A simple brand-anthem template.

videos.title: Backyard Legends
videos.note: Grassroots football in place of stadium spectacle. Heart comes from the small, specific details of kids' games.

videos.title: Cog
videos.note: A real Rube Goldberg chain of car parts in one take. Not possible to fake in one AI shot, but you can build a fake 'oner' from clips that hand off movement through hidden cuts.

videos.title: Grrr
videos.note: A bright animated world with a catchy sung hook. A strong example of an engineering message turned into joy.

videos.title: Surfer
videos.note: Surfers waiting for the perfect wave, which arrives as white horses. Strong B&W contrast and slow motion. Very achievable with AI image-to-video.

videos.title: noitulovE
videos.note: Evolution in reverse, from men back to mudskipper, in a single rewinding camera move. Reverse-time transitions are a great AI morph exercise.

videos.title: Tipping Point
videos.note: A massive domino chain through a village. Scale plus anticipation: the audience wants to see where it ends.

videos.title: Balls
videos.note: 250,000 colored balls bounce down San Francisco streets, set to a gentle acoustic song. A great reference for 'color as the product'.

videos.title: Paint
videos.note: Paint explodes across a housing block. Abstract color bursts against a drab setting is an easy contrast to borrow.

videos.title: Gorilla
videos.note: A gorilla slowly builds up to a drum fill. Almost nothing happens, then everything happens. Holding back makes the payoff bigger.

videos.title: The Force
videos.note: A kid in a costume tries to use 'the Force'; dad secretly helps with the remote start. Character want → failure → product-powered payoff, in 60s.

videos.title: The Bear & the Hare
videos.note: A hand-drawn animal fable for Christmas. A timeless storybook look that ages well.

videos.title: Man on the Moon
videos.note: A girl sees a lonely old man on the moon through a telescope. One empathetic image built into a whole campaign.

videos.title: Back to the Start
videos.note: A stop-motion farmer's journey set to a cover song. Animated brand films can carry big ideas with no dialogue.

videos.title: The Scarecrow
videos.note: A dystopian factory world with a hopeful hero. World-building that feels like a game trailer.

videos.title: The Man Your Man Could Smell Like
videos.note: A seamless single take with in-camera set changes. AI version: one continuous camera push with the world transforming behind the speaker.

videos.title: The Epic Split
videos.note: Van Damme does the splits between two reversing trucks at sunrise. One stunt, one slow reveal, one song: maximum simplicity.

videos.title: Real Beauty Sketches
videos.note: An experiment format: a hidden sketch artist and two descriptions. Documentary-style structure gives instant credibility.

videos.title: #LikeAGirl
videos.note: Ask the question on camera, let real answers carry it. Interview-led films need a twist halfway through.

videos.title: Moldy Whopper
videos.note: A 34-day timelapse of a burger rotting. A brave, ugly visual that proves the claim. Timelapse decay and growth are easy AI wins.

videos.title: Worlds Apart
videos.note: Opposites build something together before learning each other's views. A strong reveal structure.

videos.title: Chicken (Magic Body Control)
videos.note: Chickens' heads stay perfectly still while their bodies move: a product benefit shown through a natural metaphor. Find the animal or object that already 'does' your feature.

videos.title: Timeless
videos.note: A couple's love story jumps across eras in one continuous run. Era-hopping wardrobe changes suit AI style transfer.

videos.title: Kenzo World — My Mutant Brain
videos.note: An anti-perfume ad: wild, ugly-beautiful dance in an elegant venue. Break the category's clichés deliberately.

videos.title: Odyssey
videos.note: Two people smash through walls, then run up trees into the night sky. Slow motion and a classical score make it mythic.

videos.title: Circles
videos.note: Different people dancing to the same track, cut on the rhythm. Edit on the beat and shoot diverse faces.

videos.title: Parisian Love
videos.note: A love story told only through search queries. A screen-only story is cheap to make and deeply human.

videos.title: Loretta
videos.note: An old man uses the assistant to remember his late wife. Product use cases framed as memory and love.

videos.title: Gemini — New Home
videos.note: Rated the top Super Bowl LX ad by the Kellogg panel. It shows the AI imagining a new home for a family. Put the 'feature' in an emotional moment.

videos.title: Masterpiece
videos.note: Famous paintings pass a Coke from frame to frame, each in its own art style. A style-hopping relay is a perfect AI showcase.

videos.title: Happiness Factory
videos.note: The fantasy world inside a vending machine. Build a miniature universe around one ordinary object.

videos.title: Roller Babies
videos.note: CGI babies roller-skating to hip-hop. Absurd and joyful; the brand line 'live young' is acted out literally.

videos.title: Life's for Sharing — Dance
videos.note: A flash mob in a train station, filmed with hidden cameras. Spectacle captured as candid reality.

videos.title: The Fun Theory — Piano Stairs
videos.note: Turn subway stairs into a piano and watch behavior change. A great idea is often one small intervention.

videos.title: Dumb Ways to Die
videos.note: A cute characters + dark humor + catchy song formula. A safety PSA that people actually shared.

videos.title: Puppy Love
videos.note: A puppy and a Clydesdale. Pure story, no product shot needed. Animal friendship arcs work at any length.

videos.title: Lost Dog
videos.note: Lost → danger → rescue in 60s, set to a slow cover of a pop song. A classic three-act structure in miniature.

videos.title: American Icons
videos.note: One of the highest-rated spots of Super Bowl LX. Heritage imagery used with restraint.

videos.title: No.5 — The Film
videos.note: A blockbuster-scale romance for a perfume, with Nicole Kidman. Luxury storytelling: the product is a feeling, not an object.

videos.title: L'Odyssée de Cartier
videos.note: A panther travels across worlds as the brand's history. Use one recurring hero animal or object to guide the viewer through eras.

videos.title: Lamp
videos.note: A sad discarded lamp in the rain, then a guy breaks the fourth wall: 'it has no feelings'. Set up an emotion, then puncture it.

videos.title: Ostrich
videos.note: An ostrich learns to fly through VR. A 'dream unlocked by tech' arc with a clear emotional climb.

videos.title: Friends Furever
videos.note: A montage of unlikely animal friendships expresses 'be together, not the same'. Visually cheap, emotionally rich.

videos.title: Rule Yourself (Michael Phelps)
videos.note: The unglamorous grind before the glory: ice baths, cupping, dark pools. Moody low-key lighting suits AI cinematography.

videos.title: I Will What I Want (Misty Copeland)
videos.note: A rejection letter read aloud over powerful dance. Contrasting text and image creates tension.

videos.title: The Game Before the Game
videos.note: Pre-match rituals of players and fans, cut to music. A 'behind the moment' angle on a big event.

videos.title: Double Life
videos.note: Ordinary people in a row of tight portraits share one monologue about their secret gaming lives. A faces-plus-monologue format is cheap and powerful.

videos.title: Mad World
videos.note: A brutal game trailer cut to a soft, sad song. Music that works against the action creates emotion.

videos.title: The Hire
videos.note: A series of branded action short films that set the template for branded content. Look at how the car becomes a character.

videos.title: Here It Goes Again
videos.note: Treadmill choreography in a single take, made on a near-zero budget. Constraints breed ideas.

videos.title: This Too Shall Pass (Rube Goldberg)
videos.note: A warehouse-sized chain reaction synced to a song. A rhythm-synced chain reaction would make a strong AI prompt challenge.

videos.title: Lights Out
videos.note: A full horror concept in under 3 minutes with one actor and one light switch. Micro-shorts need a single rule.

videos.title: The Black Hole
videos.note: A tired office worker finds a printed black hole that steals things. A one-premise escalation ending in a karmic twist.

videos.title: Fresh Guacamole
videos.note: Everyday objects stand in for food (grenades as avocados). Visual-pun substitution is perfect for AI image generation.

videos.title: Western Spaghetti
videos.note: Bubble wrap as boiling water, Rubik's cubes as garlic. Steal the method: make a recipe out of objects that look the part.

videos.title: Pixels
videos.note: Retro game characters invade New York and pixelate it. Mash up a nostalgic style with a real setting.

videos.title: The Origin Story
videos.note: One of the first brand films made with Sora. Study how the uncanny moments are hidden with short cuts and a narrated arc.

videos.title: Air Head
videos.note: A man with a balloon for a head. The character design hides face-consistency problems, a clever AI workaround. Plan characters around the tool's limits.

videos.title: The Hardest Part
videos.note: A whole life told in one endless forward camera push. A strong idea of 'continuous zoom through time' that suits AI generation.

videos.title: NBA Finals Spot
videos.note: A fully AI ad, reportedly made in days for a tiny budget. Quick absurd vignettes with on-screen dialogue. Speed and volume beat perfection.

videos.title: Holidays Are Coming (AI)
videos.note: An AI remake of a classic, and it got plenty of backlash. Study what reads as 'soulless' (faces, warmth) and fix that in your own work.

videos.title: A.I. Ketchup
videos.note: They asked an image AI to draw 'ketchup' and it drew Heinz. Using AI as a brand-truth experiment is a meta idea you could flip.

videos.title: Pringleleo
videos.note: A Super Bowl LX standout starring Sabrina Carpenter. Celebrity plus product built into the joke itself.

videos.title: Meal Diamond
videos.note: Andy Samberg as a deli-haunting cryptid. Weird premise, total commitment.

videos.title: Bananas
videos.note: Ben Stiller and Benson Boone, directed by Spike Jonze. Look at the comic timing and musical staging.

videos.title: The Choice
videos.note: A polar bear 'defects' in a jab at a rival brand, directed by Taika Waititi. Turn a competitor's mascot against them.

videos.title: Emma Stone spot
videos.note: A deadpan, black-and-white, art-house-feeling spot with Emma Stone, directed by Yorgos Lanthimos. Bring an auteur style into a 60s ad.

videos.title: SS26
videos.note: A whole season in 45 seconds: warm, lived-in frames and zero hard sell. Let wardrobe, location and light carry the brand instead of a voiceover.

videos.title: Fall Winter 2026 campaign
videos.note: A 30-second luxury spot built on restraint. Study how few shots it needs, and how long it holds each one, to feel expensive.

videos.title: Summer 2026 by Juergen Teller
videos.note: A photographer's raw, flash-lit snapshot look moved into motion. Borrow a still photographer's style as your whole grade and framing system.

videos.title: Fall/Winter 2026 by Alex Acy
videos.note: Workwear sold through texture and real-feeling moments rather than product shots. Shoot the world the clothes live in, not the clothes.

videos.title: Warzone — Squad Up the World
videos.note: Gibson Hazard's live-action game spot for 72andSunny turns a celebrity cast into one escalating action set piece. Treat a game launch like a music-video blockbuster.

videos.title: The Negotiation
videos.note: A Super Bowl spot played as a tense two-hander. Build the whole ad around one scene of dialogue and let the brand land at the end.

videos.title: Primetime — Alternate Title Sequence
videos.note: Lance Oppenheim's scrapped opening for Primetime: Robert Pattinson as a neon ghost in a deliberately retro credits run. A title sequence can set the whole film's mood before a line is spoken.

videos.title: 550 J — Some stories are too good to stay in the archives
videos.note: A heritage launch for the electric 550 J that leans on the 1950s 550 Spyder legend. Pair archive mood with a new product to borrow decades of meaning.

videos.title: This Is America
videos.note: Hiro Murai stages chaos in the background while the performer holds the foreground in long, roaming takes. Use foreground/background contrast to say two things at once.

videos.title: Not Like Us
videos.note: A celebration staged with locals and bold, symmetrical frames. Real people and real places give a video an energy no extras can fake.

videos.title: Winter Can't Wait — by Paolo Sorrentino
videos.note: An auteur's signature (Sorrentino's grandeur and deadpan surrealism) stretched across a fashion spot. Hire a style, not just a look: let the director's world be the ad.

videos.title: Around the World
videos.note: Michel Gondry gives each instrument its own costumed group of dancers. Map every layer of the sound to something on screen and the edit almost cuts itself.

videos.title: MALAMENTE (Cap.1: Augurio)
videos.note: Flamenco iconography (bulls, motorbikes, Nazarenes) mashed with street culture in punchy, poster-like frames. Build a video from a vocabulary of strong recurring symbols.

videos.title: Point And Kill (feat. Obongjayar)
videos.note: Warm, sun-soaked frames and real locations carry the whole track. Let place and light do the heavy lifting when the performance is simple.

videos.title: FW25 — A Journey in Motion
videos.note: A collection told through motion rather than poses. Choreograph the camera and the bodies together so the clothes are always moving.

videos.title: Cracker Island (ft. Thundercat)
videos.note: Animated characters in a cinematic, lit world. AI filmmakers: study how a consistent character design survives every lighting change.

videos.title: BEHEMOTH! — Official Teaser
videos.note: A teaser that withholds more than it shows. Sell the mood and one strange image, not the plot.

videos.title: SS18 "La Bomba" — by Gordon von Steiner
videos.note: A fashion film that sells a feeling: sun, heat and the south of France, with the clothes almost incidental. Build the world first and the product lives inside it.

videos.title: Generator
videos.note: Justice's visual world in one video: bold, graphic, built to the beat. Cut to the rhythm of the track and let the music decide the edit.

videos.title: Kill Bill: The Whole Bloody Affair — Official Trailer
videos.note: A trailer for a film everyone already knows, sold on pure style: iconic frames, music and rhythm. Study how it makes the familiar feel like an event.

videos.title: "Life of a Bullet" opening sequence
videos.note: A whole opening told from the point of view of a bullet, from factory to target. Pick an unexpected POV and follow it in one unbroken journey.

videos.title: Star Guitar
videos.note: Gondry syncs every building, pole and tree passing a train window to a beat in the track. Choreograph the world to the music instead of cutting to it.

videos.title: Da Funk
videos.note: Spike Jonze ignores the song entirely and tells a deadpan short story about a dog-headed man in New York. A music video doesn't have to illustrate the track.

videos.title: Virtual Insanity
videos.note: Jonathan Glazer's moving-floor illusion: the set slides while the camera stays locked. One simple in-camera trick can carry a whole video.

videos.title: The Third Place
videos.note: David Lynch sells a console without showing it: a black-and-white dream of strange rooms and figures. Sell the feeling a product puts you in, not the product.

videos.title: R.I.P. Leon
videos.note: Cannes Film Grand Prix 2023: a pet-sitter, a lizard playing dead and one regretted text. One relatable panic moment is enough to sell a feature.

videos.title: Opening title sequence ("Harlem Shuffle")
videos.note: Edgar Wright's coffee-run oner where song lyrics appear as graffiti and signs in the street. Hide your credits and lyrics inside the world you're filming.

videos.title: Hot or Cold, Always Perfetto — Brad Pitt & 16 dogs
videos.note: Spike Jonze gives 16 dogs subtitled opinions and lets Brad Pitt play the straight man. Deadpan plus one absurd rule beats a list of product features.

videos.title: Flat Beat (with Flat Eric)
videos.note: A yellow puppet head-nodding in a car became a Levi's icon. A single, oddly specific character can be more memorable than any spectacle.

videos.title: ATHENA — Official Trailer
videos.note: Romain Gavras's riot epic, sold through huge choreographed long takes. Scale and unbroken movement make a trailer feel like an event.

videos.title: SICKO MODE (ft. Drake)
videos.note: A song in three movements, so the video changes worlds with every beat switch. When the track shifts, let the whole visual language shift with it.

videos.title: HIGHEST IN THE ROOM
videos.note: Dave Meyers builds dreamlike, gravity-free imagery around a single feeling. One strong surreal idea, pushed hard, beats ten small ones.

videos.title: The Secret Tournament ("The Cage")
videos.note: Terry Gilliam turns a football ad into a cage-match film with Eric Cantona as ringmaster. Give a sports spot a fictional world and a rulebook.

videos.title: The Denial Twist
videos.note: Gondry stretches and warps the band with in-camera tricks and funhouse optics. Practical distortion can feel more alive than digital effects.

videos.title: Go (ft. Q-Tip)
videos.note: Gondry's synchronized dancers move like machine parts through a retro-futurist city. Precise group choreography reads as graphic design in motion.

videos.title: Hideaway
videos.note: One continuous take down a Brooklyn street, built entirely on the performer's dancing. A single unbroken shot plus a magnetic performer is a full video.

videos.title: adidas is all in (Justice — "Civilization")
videos.note: Romain Gavras cuts a whole brand world to one Justice track. Let a strong song set the rhythm and the energy of an anthem film.

videos.title: Season 2 — Intro Title Sequence
videos.note: The cast performs a completely straight-faced synchronized dance as the opening credits. Absurdity played totally seriously is unforgettable.

videos.title: Season 3 — Opening Credits
videos.note: Painted, ornamental imagery hides clues about the season inside wallpaper-like motifs. A title sequence can quietly foreshadow the whole story.

videos.title: Title sequence
videos.note: Clarice running a misty training course while the credits roll: character, isolation and dread established before a word is spoken.
